findings.page: All pages (sidebar), most visible on Orders
findings.currentBehavior: The sidebar's "Sales" group has two separate entries — "Orders" (/orders) and "Awaiting Fulfillment" (/orders?status=PROCESSING) — that both route to the same OrdersPage component, the second just pre-applying a status filter. Confirmed in apps/web-admin/client/src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx lines 54-60.
findings.expectedBehavior: One "Orders" entry; "Awaiting Fulfillment" becomes a status filter/tab reachable from inside Orders, not a separate top-level nav item.
findings.recommendation: Remove the "Awaiting Fulfillment" NavItemConfig entry from NAV_GROUPS in Sidebar.tsx. Surface "Awaiting Fulfillment" as a quick-filter chip/tab inside OrdersPage.tsx instead.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only change. No backend/API change needed. Keep the fulfillment badge count but move it onto the in-page filter/tab or keep it on the "Orders" sidebar item.

findings.page: Global (Sidebar footer link, TopBar user-avatar dropdown)
findings.currentBehavior: Both logout controls are plain anchor tags (Sidebar.tsx ~line 190, TopBar.tsx ~lines 112-117) that do a GET /logout navigation. The backend logout route is POST-only (apps/web-admin/src/routes/auth.ts line 252), so the GET falls through to the SPA's catch-all and renders "Page not found" while the session cookie is never cleared. Confirmed: after clicking Logout, /orders still loads authenticated.
findings.expectedBehavior: Clicking Logout ends the session and returns the admin to /login.
findings.recommendation: Change both logout controls to issue a POST /logout via fetch, then redirect to /login on success.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only fix — backend route already correct. Consider a shared logout() helper in apps/web-admin/client/src/api/client.ts.

findings.currentBehavior: The Status filter combobox on Orders lists all 13 order statuses verbatim as backend enum identifiers (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE), e.g. "PAYMENT_DETECTED", "PENDING_VERIFICATION".
findings.expectedBehavior: Human-readable labels, e.g. "Payment Detected", "Pending Verification", ideally grouped/ordered by the customer journey.
findings.recommendation: Add a label map (ORDER_STATUS_LABELS) in OrdersPage.tsx or a shared lib/orderStatus.ts and render labels instead of raw enum values in both the filter dropdown and the table's Status column/badges.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only. No backend change — purely a display-label mapping.

findings.currentBehavior: Every row's "Admin" column renders the raw internal user id (e.g. 1) instead of the admin's name/username.
findings.expectedBehavior: Show the admin's username/name, with the numeric ID available as a tooltip or secondary detail if needed.
findings.recommendation: Join admin username/name into the audit log API response (or resolve client-side from an already-fetched admins list) and render that instead of the bare ID.
findings.implementationNotes: May need a small backend change (include admin name in the audit log query/response) — borderline in-scope, triage in phase 2.

findings.currentBehavior: TopBar.tsx renders the search trigger button with icon, label span, and kbd hint, but the button itself has no aria-label. Below the sm breakpoint the label/hint are hidden via Tailwind, leaving an unnamed icon-only button for screen readers. Confirmed via accessibility snapshot at 375px width. Source: apps/web-admin/client/src/components/layout/TopBar.tsx lines 41-51.
findings.expectedBehavior: The search button always has a discoverable accessible name, regardless of viewport.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label="Search" to the button element itself.

findings.currentBehavior: Settings renders 9+ sections top to bottom in a single column with no in-page navigation: General, Telegram & Bot, TokoPay, PayDisini, NOWPayments, Bybit, Bybit BSC, Binance Internal Transfer, Exchange Rates, Security. To reach Security an admin must scroll past 8 other sections. No anchor links, tabs, or sticky section index.
findings.expectedBehavior: Sectioned navigation (tabs, a sticky in-page sidebar, or anchor links/a "jump to" control) so admins can reach a specific section without scrolling through everything else.
findings.recommendation: Add a sticky section nav that scrolls to/highlights the active section, or split into tabs (General / Payments / Security). Preserve the current whitelist-only edit behavior — do not widen it.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only, structural. No new fields, no whitelist change.

findings.currentBehavior: With no filter applied (fresh DB, zero orders), the empty state reads "No orders found / Try adjusting your filters." — wrong/confusing when there is no filter active at all.
findings.expectedBehavior: Context-aware messaging: "No orders yet" (no data, no filter) vs. "No orders match these filters" + a "Clear filters" action when a filter is actually narrowing an otherwise-populated set.
findings.recommendation: Branch the empty-state copy in OrdersPage.tsx on whether any filter (status, search, date range) is currently active.

findings.currentBehavior: The Action column renders backend action codes verbatim (denomination_create, catalog_product_create, category_create, web_setup_completed), redundant next to the already-readable Details sentence.
findings.expectedBehavior: A human-readable action label, or the raw code column de-emphasized/removed since Details already carries the readable sentence.
findings.recommendation: Add a label map for known action codes, or drop the column in favor of a small icon/badge derived from the action category plus the existing Details sentence.

findings.currentBehavior: "Add a new X" is implemented three different ways: Products/Denominations use a dedicated full page; Vouchers expands an inline form section above the table; Admins uses a single-row inline form built into the table header with no labels on additional fields.
findings.expectedBehavior: One consistent creation pattern for records of similar complexity, or at minimum two clear tiers applied consistently.
findings.recommendation: Keep the dedicated-page pattern for multi-field records (Product, Denomination); use the inline expand-in-place pattern (Vouchers' approach) for simpler ones (Voucher, Admin) rather than Admins' single-field table-row variant.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only. No backend change — same create endpoints, different presentation only.

findings.currentBehavior: The breadcrumb reads "Catalog / Product" — the literal word "Product" is rendered as link text instead of the actual product name. Confirmed via accessibility snapshot.
findings.expectedBehavior: Breadcrumb shows the real product name, e.g. "Catalog / Netflix Premium / New Denomination".
findings.recommendation: Pass the loaded product's name into the breadcrumb component instead of a hardcoded "Product" string; handle the loading state properly.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only. Likely also affects DenominationEditPage.tsx — verify in phase 2.

findings.currentBehavior: Only two real heading elements exist on the Dashboard (H1 Dashboard, H2 Operation Center). Visually-heading-styled section titles (Critical Stock, Upcoming Expirations, Sales Analytics, Recent Orders, Business Health, Top Products) are plain div/span elements, not h2/h3 tags. Confirmed via document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6').
findings.expectedBehavior: Each dashboard card/section title is a real heading element so screen-reader users can navigate by heading structure.
findings.recommendation: Change section-title elements to semantic heading tags, keeping existing visual styling via the same CSS classes.

findings.currentBehavior: Measured via getComputedStyle: the "Search..." label renders as rgb(151, 161, 177) on a transparent/light background, ~2.6:1 contrast ratio — below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for normal text.
findings.expectedBehavior: Muted/secondary text meets at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background (or qualifies for the 3:1 large-text threshold).
findings.recommendation: Darken the muted text color token and audit other uses of the same utility class for the same issue, with an actual contrast-checker pass in phase 2.
findings.implementationNotes: Likely a shared Tailwind/theme token change, not a one-off. Needs a broader grep before fixing. Preserve existing brand colors — adjust only the token's lightness enough to pass contrast.

findings.currentBehavior: Every payment gateway section shows a "not configured" label right next to an "Enabled" switch that is toggled on by default, with all credential fields "not set" — reads as contradictory.
findings.expectedBehavior: Visual state should make it obvious that "Enabled + not configured" effectively means "inactive".
findings.recommendation: Derive a single combined status label/badge from enabled && hasRequiredFields instead of showing two seemingly contradictory signals.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only. Confirm with product owner whether "Enabled" defaulting to true pre-setup is intentional business logic (out of scope) — this finding is about display only.

findings.currentBehavior: The inline voucher-creation form relies on placeholder-only text (or, for one combobox, no label at all — confirmed via accessibility snapshot). Inconsistent with Product/Denomination create forms, which use a clear Label + helper-text pattern.
findings.expectedBehavior: Every field has a persistent visible label, consistent with the rest of the app's forms.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same Label + Input/Select composition already used in ProductCreatePage.tsx/DenominationCreatePage.tsx to the voucher inline form.

findings.page: Product Create, Denomination Create, Product Detail
findings.currentBehavior: These pages show both a breadcrumb link in the top-left and a separate "← Back" button in the top-right, doing the same job.
findings.recommendation: Keep the breadcrumb (it also communicates hierarchy) and drop the redundant "← Back" button, or merge them.
findings.implementationNotes: UI-only, low risk. Check apps/web-admin/client/src/components/shared/PageHeader.tsx and/or PageLayout.tsx for where this pattern is defined once.

findings.currentBehavior: The Admins table has a column header literally labeled "Pwd".
findings.expectedBehavior: A clearer label, e.g. "Password Set" or a tooltip-bearing icon.
findings.recommendation: Rename the header text (and/or add a title attribute / tooltip).

findings.currentBehavior: Searching "Netflix" with a product named "Netflix Premium" existing in the DB returned "No results for 'Netflix'". Confirmed the request reached the backend and returned 200 OK with an empty result set.
findings.expectedBehavior: The product appears in search results.
findings.implementationNotes: Likely backend/business-logic work, out of scope for UI-only phase 2 — schedule separately. Needs backend investigation before any UI change is relevant.

findings.currentBehavior: On the 7-day Sales Analytics chart at 375px width, one date label (07-13) does not appear in the accessibility tree, while all 7 dates render at desktop width. Could be intentional label-thinning or a genuine bug — pattern looked inconsistent with simple thinning rules.
findings.expectedBehavior: Either a clearly intentional, evenly-spaced label thinning strategy on narrow viewports, or all 7 labels retained with smaller text/rotation.
findings.recommendation: Re-verify directly in the chart library's own responsive tick logic in phase 2 before changing anything.
findings.implementationNotes: Low priority — verify before investing implementation time.
